item.title: Brain Damage in Schizophrenia May Begin in Specific Neural Epicenters - Neuroscience News
item.description: New brain imaging research shows that structural damage in schizophrenia spectrum disorders may begin in specific “epicenter” regions before spreading across connected brain networks.

item.title: Watching Pain on Screen Can Make Your Body Flinch - Neuroscience News
item.description: Watching someone experience pain on screen activates your own brain’s touch-processing system in a highly organized, body-specific way.

item.title: CBD Can Reduce Aggression in Dogs - Neuroscience News
item.description: A massive multi-year analysis of tens of thousands of dogs reveals that CBD use is becoming increasingly common among aging companion animals.

item.title: Neural Ultrasound Boosts Learning in 60 Seconds - Neuroscience News
item.description: Researchers have successfully altered human reward learning using non-invasive transcranial ultrasound stimulation directed at a deep brain structure linked to motivation.

item.title: The Way You Drive Might Signal Mild Cognitive Impairment - Neuroscience News
item.description: Researchers found that long-term driving behavior can reveal early signs of cognitive decline years before clinical diagnosis.

item.title: Singing Mice Reveal How Brains Evolved for Vocal Speech - Neuroscience News
item.description: Alston’s singing mice produce loud, rhythmic songs that scientists can clearly hear, alongside ultrasonic calls used for close-range communication.

item.title: Insomnia Keeps the Brain Stuck in Daytime Mode - Neuroscience News
item.description: People with chronic insomnia show a delayed and weakened daily rhythm of mental activity, keeping the brain in a more alert, daytime-like state at night.

item.title: Scientists Achieve Sustained HIV Control Without Lifelong Drugs - Neuroscience News
item.description: Scientists tested a multi-step immune-based therapy designed to retrain the body to control HIV without continuous antiviral treatment.

item.title: AI Watches Pianists and Reconstructs Their Muscle Signals - Neuroscience News
item.description: Researchers developed an AI system that can reconstruct fine hand muscle activity using only standard video footage.

item.title: Smelling Fatty Foods in Pregnancy May Raise Obesity Risk in Children - Neuroscience News
item.description: New research shows that exposure to the smell of fatty foods during pregnancy and early life can reprogram the developing brain and increase the risk of obesity and insulin resistance in adulthood.
